# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 23:30 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 249 active entries of tips_notebook.json (46 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- Ballots are secret, so keep a notepad: for every nomination and trial, log each player's stated vote, the announced totals and your own vote. Flag stated votes that later change, contradict the player's reads or don't fit the totals.
- Totals can be changed on purpose. A Ballot Stuffer makes a trial total exceed the voter count, and a Fixer silently flips one player's trial votes. Neither touches nomination votes, so a Yes count that contradicts stated votes is the cleanest proof of a liar; list the fix and stuffer accounts before accusing on trial totals.
- Keep your votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before the vote. A read/vote mismatch in others is a lead, not a verdict. (seen in 30 games)
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. Still, a corroborated lone unexplained visitor to a Katana victim is near-proof against them; don't let 'a visit isn't an attack' acquit them. (seen in 29 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat unless Unique. But 'roles can repeat' only means a claim isn't disproved; it is not evidence for it. (seen in 28 games)
- Before each night, write your planned target in your will, and post results publicly by day. The result of the night you die never reaches your will. (seen in 27 games)
- Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked. Evasion becomes its own case. (seen in 7 games)
- Tokens are useless once you're dead. Spend one-shot tokens on the first Day or night they can change a vote or remove a threat. A puppet or doubled ballot lapses if you die the night you spend it.

## Village
- Investigators: post your role, night, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it. If someone copies your claim, counterclaim at once with your full log. (seen in 16 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name a concrete contradiction or mechanical fit: an Evil result against a Vanilla claim, a group elimination, or a lone visitor. If the nominee self-nominated, wants the rope, or the case is only behavioural, run the Jester check first. (seen in 32 games)
- If the nominee wins by being hanged, leave them alive. If you must hang a possible Jester, agree on a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles on Innocent. (seen in 15 games)
- Once a player is shown Yakuza by a mechanical result, suspect those who argued for No or delay, or who PM'd them. Ask for stated votes before each vote and compare them with the Yes count. A PM link alone is a lead, never a hang. (seen in 28 games)
- On Day 2 don't hint at protective roles or tokens. Never announce tonight's target, in public or by PM; that tells the Pharmacist and the Katana where to go. (seen in 24 games)
- Hunt Neutral killers on purpose. A cause of death not explained by the Katana or known shooters, a multi-death night, or an unexplained survival means one is alive. Point checks at unwatched Vanilla and unclaimed players, and hang the best suspect before you are down to two players.
- Survival confirms nothing: Arsonists and Serial Killers have Standard Defense, and Jesters and Executioners have Basic. Ask the survivor which protector explains it. (seen in 15 games)
- An archive is a sample, not a census: about half the entries are fake. Use it to decide whom to press and test, then hang on the contradiction the test produces. (seen in 14 games)

## Yakuza
- Never PM teammates by day; plan everything in night chat. An Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads PMs, and PM triangles become the town's lead. (seen in 30 games)
- Don't defend a doomed teammate unless your team's votes can actually save them. Otherwise vote with the town. On a likely Jester, keep some teammates on Innocent to stay out of the revenge draw. (seen in 34 games)
- Every member submits the agreed Katana holder and target every night. With two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 19 games)
- Fake-claim a Village role whose tokens match yours. Never claim a Yakuza-only role, a Unique role or a role already claimed in public. Fix each member's claim before Day 2 and never switch it. (seen in 18 games)
- Give the Katana to your least useful member. Move it to an unexposed member the night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder, and kill info roles whose results are narrowing your options. (seen in 21 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit someone could have seen. Admit it at once with a cover story agreed in night chat. (seen in 15 games)
- After a failed attack, kill or block the likely protector instead of retrying. Use the rig and puppet early, but never rig a Day when a teammate is the likely nominee. (seen in 19 games)
- Smuggler swaps move exactly the actions aimed at the two swapped players. Aim the Katana at a decoy and swap the decoy with the protected real target, or swap yourself with a Villager to dodge a check. Never swap the Katana's target by accident.

## Sheriff
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night. Say so whenever you post a Not Evil result. (seen in 16 games)

## Coroner
- Examine bodies that settle a live question: one side of a duplicate claim, a hanged suspect, or a possibly forged will. Post night, target and role in one message. Skip cleaned bodies, which show nothing.

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana. Protect vocal analysts and claimed investigators, rotate among them, and self-protect with a token right after you claim. (seen in 21 games)

## Vigilante
- Don't die holding your shots. Set a trigger by Day 2-3 and fire a Basic shot on a solid lead, then post the night, target and role if it kills. (seen in 11 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more living players are doused, or with 2 if anyone is questioning you. Every night spent dousing is a night the town can hang you first. (seen in 12 games)

task: It is Night 1. Yakuza chat, round 1 of at most 3. Discuss tonight's plan: who holds the Katana, who it attacks, and your other actions. There is no attack unless at least 2 of the 3 living Yakuza vote for the same target. The holder vote is separate: the Katana moves only if at least 2 vote for the same new holder, and otherwise the current holder keeps it and makes any attack. Send a message (max 200 words; longer is truncated) or null. Set ready=true if you have nothing more to discuss; chat ends when everyone is ready.

answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing seemed broken. I cross-checked every Fortune Teller count and Cartographer size against the revealed night actions (N1-N4), and all were consistent. Frank (Diviner, Katana holder) targeted the same player with both actions on N4, and his role-block correctly stopped both. answers.suggestions: (1) Add an optional auto-ledger of stated votes per trial, or let players tag a public message as a vote statement so it is logged. (3) Add one clarifying sentence to the Census Taker text: 'Outsiders such as the Roleplayer and Ex-Con count as Good.' (4) Raise the notepad cap slightly for long games.

A one-line note would help: 'claiming a Neutral role implies a non-Village faction is still alive whenever the game hasn't ended.' That makes the decoys real evidence that those roles exist. My N1 decoys (Diviner, Wiretap) proved two Yakuza roles were in play, and my N2 decoy Ballot Stuffer proved a Ballot Stuffer existed. But the rule also says 'a listed role is not proof that anyone in the game has it'. That warning seems to apply only in the fallback case, and it is not stated clearly when the fallback triggers. A one-line note in the result saying whether the decoys came from in-play roles would remove the ambiguity. Also, the setup says every non-Vanilla role is unique, while R2 says only Smuggler and Vulture are unique. Players used the setup line to disprove Frank's Oracle double-claim. It took a moment to see that the setup rule overrides R2 for this game.

I tracked these by hand from the log: who holds the Katana after each move or pass, each player's remaining tokens, especially when a block refunds a token (Heidi's ballot token twice), the seat circle after deaths (for Diviner, Surveyor and Census neighbours), and the full visit graph each night. answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to generate the visit graph and the derived results (Fortune Teller, Cartographer, Scout, Insomniac) automatically from the submitted actions, rather than by hand. I also wanted to post a separate public metadata event for each private message, so that 'Erin sent Grace a private message' is visibly broadcast to everyone, not only tagged with its content recipients.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: 1) The Fortune Teller got Night 1 numbers although Day 2 is the first Day; see confusing_rules. 2) The Ex-Con's notifications were inconsistent: Ivan was told 'you made your automatic visit' only on Night 3, and got nothing on Nights 1, 2 and 4. 3) The phrasing of night-result messages drifted: 'Night 2 result:' prefixes on some nights and not others, 'nobody visited her last night' delivered during the night itself, and Frank's 'You were role-blocked last night'. 4) The log shows Erin's private message to Grace only to Bob, Erin and Grace. Under R4 everyone should see that a message was sent; I couldn't confirm the public notice went out. 5) Nothing else seemed broken. The win check after Frank's hanging, the Katana passes, Heidi's unspent tokens and the trial totals (11 and 10 votes, no doubled ballot) were all consistent.
answers.suggestions: 1) Make the Fortune Teller rule explicit: either 'every Day, starting Day 2, about the previous Night' or 'not on Day 2'. 2) Give the moderator an auto-maintained state panel: Katana holder, token ledger, circle order, block and immunity status, and a computed visit graph with the Fortune Teller, Cartographer and Scout outputs pre-filled for checking. 3) Standardise the night-result templates, including a fixed nightly line for automatic actions such as the Ex-Con's visit. 4) Show the public private-message notice as its own log event. 5) Add worked examples to R8 for a blocked new holder and for the holder's own action on the same target.

task:

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Spend map tokens on the player at the center of the live dispute, such as the Katana suspect or a claimed blocker. Then cross the exact group membership with the Fortune Teller's visited/visitor counts. Group size plus the FT counts pins down who the hidden visitor must be, and that turned a Lookout's word into a mechanical case.

When a player claims Jester or Executioner on trial, check the win condition. If the game didn't end after the last known Evil died, someone non-Village is still alive. Pair that with whether a kill happened on the night the claimant was blocked. A no-kill night right when the suspect was blocked is strong evidence that they hold the Katana.

Profiler fakes are drawn from other players' real roles. So a profile list that settles one player's role also proves the other listed roles are in play. Use this to list the likely Yakuza roles (e.g. Diviner, Wiretap, Ballot Stuffer) and check them off as players die.

Don't double-claim a unique info role like Oracle on Day 2 before the real holder has spoken. It forces an immediate counterclaim fight you lose to any census or profile, and the fallback claims (Roleplayer, then Jester) read as foreknowledge.
Keep a cheap repeating block (Party Animal) on the top Katana suspect every night once they are identified. Three straight blocks produced no-kill nights, which confirmed the holder.

tips_feedback.tip: Never PM teammates by day; plan everything in night chat. An Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads PMs.

tips_feedback.why: Grace's PM'd plan got her killed, and Heidi's public 'I'll check Mallory' got her blocked. Both show why announcing targets is costly.

tips_feedback.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action. Still, a corroborated lone unexplained visitor to a Katana victim is near-proof against them.
tips_feedback.why: Erin's lone-visitor sighting of Bob at Grace, corroborated by my map and Carol's counts, led to a correct hang despite Bob's 'it's only Erin's word' defense.

tips_feedback.tip: If the nominee self-nominated, wants the rope, or the case is only behavioural, run the Jester check first.
tips_feedback.why: We ran the Jester check on Frank's trial claim using mechanics: the game hadn't ended after Heidi died, and there was no kill the night he was blocked. That let us hang him with confidence, and the game ended with our win.

tips_feedback.tip: Fake-claim a Village role whose tokens match yours. Never claim a Yakuza-only role, a Unique role or a role already claimed in public.
tips_feedback.why: Frank broke it by claiming Oracle against the real Oracle, which immediately made him a suspect. Heidi's Sheriff claim was later disproved by a profile. Breaking the advice clearly hurt the Yakuza.

summary: The Village won 10-3 with no Village losses after Night 2. Three things decided the game. First, Alice's Census Taker results count true alignment, and Carol, Dave and Mallory confirmed them on themselves, so the census became the trusted backbone of every case. Second, Mallory's Party Animal blocks landed on the Katana holder on Night 3 (Heidi) and Night 4 (Frank), cancelling two of the Yakuza's four kills. Third, Erin's Lookout watches produced two lone-visitor cases: Heidi at Judy on N1, and Bob at Grace on N2. The Yakuza hurt themselves badly. Frank fake-claimed Oracle, a unique role the real Oracle (Grace) then claimed, and was forced into a 'Roleplayer' retreat. Heidi claimed Sheriff and announced she would check Mallory, which gave Mallory a public reason to block her every night. On N2 Bob correctly read Erin's PM plan through the Wiretap and killed Grace, but Erin was watching Grace and caught him. On N3 the Katana was moved to Heidi, who was already being blocked nightly, so the night was wasted. Frank's final Jester claim failed on mechanics: the game hadn't ended when Heidi died, and the night he was blocked had no kill.

issues.description: The Fortune Teller rule says the numbers arrive 'at the start of each Day except the first'. Since the game starts with Night 1 and the first Day is Day 2, a literal reading gives no numbers on Day 2. The harness gave Carol her Night 1 numbers anyway, delivered at night and labelled 'read at the start of Day 2'. The 'except the first' clause looks like leftover wording from a version that had a Day 1, and should be removed or clarified.

Ivan (Ex-Con) was sent a notice about his automatic visit only on Night 3 ('You made your automatic Ex-Con visit to a random player'). He got nothing on Nights 1, 2 or 4. Ivan flagged in feedback that his night history was incomplete. Automatic-action notices should be consistent every night.
